_comment: The design questions: requirements that ask how the system is built, which the owner knows and no scanner reaches. Answered in securevibe.toml's [design] section as yes, no, or not-sure, with `where` naming the file that does it. An answer of yes is *attested by the owner* — the weakest tier there is, and never evidence that the control is really there, because the owner asserting a property is not the property. An answer of no is a finding: the owner has said the control is missing. `where` pointing at a file that is not in the app is a finding too, because a stale pointer is worse than none. Each question's words are read against its requirement by crates/sv-check/tests/design.rs, the same way the security notes are.

questions.title: Input validation is enforced at a trusted service layer
questions.asks: Does the application enforce input validation on the server — a trusted service layer — and not only in the browser? Client-side validation improves usability and should be kept, but anyone can skip it by sending a request straight to the server, so it settles nothing on its own.
questions.whereMeans: the file where input validation happens on the server

questions.title: Session tokens are verified by a trusted backend service
questions.asks: Does the application perform all session token verification using a trusted backend service, rather than believing something the browser sends about who is signed in?
questions.whereMeans: the file where the session is verified

questions.title: Authorization rules are enforced at a trusted service layer
questions.asks: Does the application enforce its authorization rules at a trusted service layer — the server — rather than relying on controls an untrusted consumer could manipulate, such as a hidden button or a disabled field in the browser? Hiding a link is not a rule: anyone can request the address directly.
questions.whereMeans: the file where authorization is enforced

questions.title: Only the fields that are needed are sent back
questions.asks: When the application returns a record, does it return only the required fields, rather than the whole object with fields the person should not see?
questions.whereMeans: the file that decides which fields are returned

questions.title: Input is decoded once, before it is checked
questions.asks: Is input decoded or unescaped into its final form exactly once, and before it is validated, rather than after? Decoding after the check lets something dangerous slip past a check that saw it encoded.

questions.title: Headers added by a load balancer cannot be faked
questions.asks: If a load balancer, proxy, or gateway sits in front of the application and adds header fields it relies on, can the application tell those apart from the same fields sent by a browser?
questions.whereMeans: the file or configuration that handles those header fields

questions.title: Everything in front of the app agrees where a request ends
questions.asks: Do all the components a request passes through — load balancers, firewalls, and the application server — agree on where one HTTP message ends and the next begins? When they disagree, somebody can hide a second request inside the first.
questions.whereMeans: the configuration for the server or proxy in front of the app

questions.title: Access to individual fields is restricted
questions.asks: Where some fields of a record are more restricted than the record itself, does the application check permissions for those specific fields, both when read and when written?
questions.whereMeans: the file that enforces field-level permissions

questions.title: Tokens go only where they are needed
questions.asks: Are access tokens sent only to the components that strictly need them, rather than handed to the browser when the server could hold them instead?

questions.title: Encryption choices can be changed later
questions.asks: Is the application designed so the algorithms, key lengths, and random number sources it uses for encryption and hashing can be replaced without rewriting it? Every algorithm in use now will eventually need replacing.
questions.whereMeans: the file where the algorithms are chosen

questions.title: Calls between the app's own backend components are authenticated
questions.asks: Where communications between backend application components — APIs, middleware, and data layers — do not carry the standard user session, is each call authenticated, so a caller has to prove who it is rather than merely being able to reach the address?
questions.whereMeans: the file where calls between services are authenticated

questions.title: Accounts used between the app's own parts have the least privilege needed
questions.asks: Are communications between backend application components — local or operating system services, APIs, middleware, and data layers — performed with accounts assigned the least privileges necessary for each one, rather than one powerful account used everywhere because it is simpler?
questions.whereMeans: the configuration that sets up those accounts

questions.title: Sensitive data is not left in a cache
questions.asks: Does the application prevent sensitive data from being kept in caches it does not own — a load balancer, a content delivery network, or an application cache — or make sure anything kept there is protected?
questions.whereMeans: the file or configuration that sets caching

questions.title: The visitor's real address is passed along truthfully
questions.asks: If proxies or middleware sit in front of the application, do they pass the visitor's original IP address in a field the visitor cannot set themselves? Rate limits and logs are worth nothing if the address can be chosen by whoever is being limited.
questions.whereMeans: the proxy configuration, or the file that reads the address

questions.title: Clocks agree, and times say which zone they are in
questions.asks: Do all the parts of the application that write logs keep their clocks synchronized, and do the timestamps use UTC or say which time zone they are in? Two logs with drifting clocks cannot be put in order after an incident.

questions.title: Logs are sent somewhere separate
questions.asks: Are logs sent to a separate system, so that somebody who takes over the application cannot quietly delete the record of what they did?
questions.whereMeans: the configuration that ships the logs
